chapter: After the Army: JATP, clubs and first Europe trips
title: Deciding to go to Europe in 1949
summary: After years of hearing about Paris, he saved money to go with drummer Wallace Bishop and trumpeter Merle Stepter.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes. When did you first go to Europe?

Well another case like in California. I wanted to come to New York from California, I'd heard so much about it. So now, I'd heard so much about it, England and France and people would come back when I was in the Teresa, like Joe Louis would go there on exhibition boxing tours, he'd say 'Buck, you don't believe it, you've got to go over there and see.' And other people

would tell me. Everybody told me about Paris and London. So I just saved up enough money. No I didn't either. Yes I did. This is the first time. I saved my own money. Me and Earl Hines' drummer, Bishop, Wallace Bishop and another trumpet player which I didn't need, but he and I were close friends. We all saved up enough money.
Well where does he come from?
Ohio. I don't know where he is now.
